string.text: Click, then press a key to bind it.
Optional modifier held with the identify key.
Card (full details), Minimal (a faction-coloured dot with a relation sign), or Bodycam (a faction-coloured outline box locked to the head).
Bodycam style: draw the outline rectangle around just the head/face, or around the full body.
Bodycam style: colour the outline rectangle by faction, or by relationship (red enemy / green friendly / grey neutral).
Bodycam style: thickness of the outline rectangle's edges, in pixels.
Bodycam style: extra margin around the model so the outline isn't tight against it. A fraction of the box size (0 = tight, 0.20 = 20% larger each side), so it stays proportional at any distance.
Bodycam style: opacity of the outline rectangle (1 = solid, lower = more transparent). The name/faction/weapon text is unaffected.
Continuously identify every visible target in range without pressing the key. Line of sight is always required. Pairs well with the Bodycam style.

Draw a distortion over just the FACE of every humanoid in range -- ALIVE or dead. Independent of identification -- no need to aim at or identify anyone. The box sits over the front of the head (the face). Requires the custom bodycam engine build; inert without it.
How a face is redacted: a pixelated (mosaic) censor, or a solid black box.
Extra margin around the face box, as a fraction of its size (0 = tight on the face, 0.15 = 15% larger each side).

How far face redaction reaches. Independent of the identify Max range -- redaction is passive, so it can reach further than you can aim-identify. A distant face still stops once it's under ~1px on screen.
Master intensity of the redaction effect.
Tint the tag by your relation to the target: red enemy, green friend, tan neutral.
Show the target's name line. Applies to every style that draws text (Card and Bodycam).
Show the target's faction line. Applies to every style that draws text (Card and Bodycam).
Show the target's currently-wielded weapon and its caliber. Applies to every style that draws text (Card and Bodycam).
Skip the scan wait and spinner entirely -- the tag reveals immediately on identify. Overrides Scan delay and all its distance/rank/darkness modifiers.
How long the scan pulses before the tag reveals.
Fade in/out duration of the tag.
How long the tag stays fully visible after identification (while the target remains in sight; out-of-sight targets drop sooner, see "Drop tag when out of sight").
Range at which the tag starts fading out with distance.
When you don't land a direct hit, identify the nearest target within the on-screen assist circle. Turn off to require aiming directly at the target.
For bodycam / free-aim engines: center the assist circle on where the weapon actually points instead of the screen center. Leave off on a normal engine.
Aim tolerance for picking a target without a direct hit. Measured as an angle from where you aim, so it works the same whether hip-firing or scoped at any magnification (0 = direct hit only).
Only pick targets you can actually see.
Drop tag when out of sight

Remove an active tag as soon as its target goes out of sight (behind cover or off-screen), instead of waiting out the visibility duration. A brief occlusion is tolerated; re-identify (or auto-identify) brings it back.
Also auto-identify on a steady aim through raised binoculars, alongside the normal key.
Identification only works while actively looking through raised binoculars.
How long to hold aim steady before auto-identifying.
Whether FOV target assist also applies while looking through raised binoculars. Turn off to require a direct hit when using binoculars.
Faster reveal and longer range with binoculars raised, any mode.
Scan speed multiplier while binoculars are raised.
Max (and fade-out) distance multiplier while binoculars are raised. A flat multiplier by default, or the x1 base when "Scale range by magnification" (below) is on.

Multiply the binocular range by the binocular's magnification (like the ADS option), so the range tracks the optical zoom instead of a flat multiplier. Off = flat "Binoculars max distance multiplier". On: set that multiplier to 1.0 for range = base x magnification.
Also auto-identify on a steady aim while aiming down sight, alongside the normal key.
Faster reveal and longer range while aiming down sight, any mode.
Scan speed multiplier while aiming down sight (lower = faster).
Max (and fade-out) distance multiplier while aiming down sight. This is the base for a 1x sight; higher-power scopes scale it up if zoom scaling is on.

Multiply the ADS range by the scope's magnification (x2, x4, ...), so higher-power optics reach further. Works with PiP scopes and, on engines without PiP, from the aim FOV. Iron sights stay near the x1 base.
While aiming down sight, suppress all main-view drawing (identification tags and main-view redaction) for a clean sight picture. In-scope markers/redaction (if any) still draw.
Draw identification markers inside a Picture-in-Picture scope's lens. Needs a PiP-capable engine; when off, the mod behaves as if there were no PiP support (normal HUD, no in-scope markers).
Draw the dead-body redaction effect inside a PiP scope's lens too. Independent of the markers toggle; the main-view redaction is unaffected either way.
Hide main-view UI when scope is up
While a PiP scope is rendering, suppress all main-view drawing (identification tags and main-view redaction), leaving only the in-scope UI.
Flat size multiplier for the whole card. Not distance-based.
Below this scale, show just the relation dot instead of the full card.
Further targets take longer to scan.
Scan time multiplier at max range. Binoculars mitigate this for free by extending max range itself.
Higher-ranked stalkers take longer to identify than a rookie.
Scan time multiplier for the highest rank (legend), vs. a rookie.
Targets are harder to make out in the dark; the slowdown ramps up over dusk and peaks in the dead of night (around 0:00).
Scan time multiplier at the darkest point of the night, vs. broad daylight.
Re-identifying someone you've identified before is faster.
Scan time multiplier for a previously-identified target.
Identifying gets faster with a higher Skill System perception level (needs the optional FOMOD component).
Scan time reduction per perception level.
Perception experience granted on a successful identify.
Bonus perception experience granted the first time you loot a corpse you'd already identified.
Write aim/trace diagnostics to the game log (xray_*.log) on each identify attempt. For troubleshooting free-aim target acquisition. Leave off normally.

On-screen visualiser for the FOV target-assist: a RED dot at the current aim point, a YELLOW ring showing the assist radius (fov_radius, with its value as text), and dots on the bones of every entity whose body falls inside the ring -- GREEN if within identify range, RED if the target is beyond max range -- each labelled with its distance in metres. Also shows the current scope magnification and the effective max range (base widened by the binocular/ADS boost). For tuning fov_radius / max range / diagnosing target acquisition. Leave off normally.
